title: Every turn of a hint ladder stays visible
statement: Through a hint sequence, keep every earlier answer and hint on screen, since a hint that builds on the last answer is useless once that answer is gone.
detail: A reading course runs a typed or spoken open answer as a conversation of three scored turns, a hint, a closer hint and then the answer, and its rule keeps every turn on screen, so the child can see what they already said and what they were already told (`grade3-reading/course-renderer/docs/rules/questions-and-assessment.md`, lines 403-420). A hint written to build on the last answer works only while that answer is still there to read.

evidence.quote: Every turn stays on screen. The child can see what they already said and what they were already told, because a hint that builds on their last answer is useless beside an empty box where that answer used to be.
**Rule.** A typed or spoken open response is a conversation with three scored turns, and the reply escalates on each one.

Every turn stays on screen. The child can see what they already said and what they were already told, because a hint that builds on their last answer is useless beside an empty box where that answer used to be.
A criterion met on any turn stays met for the rest of the question.
